articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Establishes the five fundamental principles (integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality, professional behavior) and the conceptual framework for all professional accountants in business (Part 2) and public practice (Part 3), incorporating 2026 external expert and sustainability reporting revisions.

articles.heading: Five Fundamental Principles, Threats & 2026 External Expert Rules
articles.text:
• Five Fundamental Principles (Section 110): Integrity, Objectivity, Professional Competence and Due Care, Confidentiality, and Professional Behavior.
• Five Threat Categories (Section 120): Self-interest, Self-review, Advocacy, Familiarity, and Intimidation — addressed by eliminating circumstances, applying safeguards, or declining/ending the engagement.
• NOCLAR (Sections 260 & 360): structured response framework for Non-Compliance with Laws and Regulations.
• 2026 Handbook Additions (effective 15 Dec 2026): new Section 290 (PAIBs) and Section 390 (PAPPs) governing ethical evaluation when using the work of an external expert, plus sustainability reporting ethics revisions.

articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Sets out the International Independence Standards applicable to audit and review engagements, including public interest entity (PIE) definitions, fee-related provisions, non-assurance services restrictions, and partner rotation.

articles.heading: Audit & Review Independence: PIEs, Fees, NAS & Partner Rotation
articles.text:
• Independence of Mind and Independence in Appearance required throughout the engagement period and period covered by the financial statements (Section 400).
• Public Interest Entities — PIEs (Section 400.17): expanded definition covering publicly traded entities, banks, insurers, and entities holding assets in a fiduciary capacity.
• Fee-related provisions (Section 410): public fee transparency for PIEs and fee-dependency thresholds (>15% for 2 consecutive years triggers mandatory pre-issuance EQR; >15% for 5 consecutive years triggers resignation for PIEs).
• Non-Assurance Services — NAS (Section 600): prohibits creating a self-review threat for PIE audit clients (no materiality qualifier) and requires TCWG concurrence; Key Audit Partner rotation limited to 7 years on / 5 years cooling-off for PIE engagement partners (Section 540).

articles.heading: Scope & Key Requirements (Public Summary)
articles.text: Sets out independence standards for assurance engagements other than audit, review, and sustainability assurance engagements covered by Part 5.

articles.heading: Independence for Other Assurance Engagements
articles.text:
• Applies to assurance engagements other than audits/reviews of historical financial statements (Part 4A) and sustainability assurance engagements (Part 5 — IESSA).
• Covers financial interests, loans/guarantees, business/family relationships, long association, and provision of non-assurance services to assurance clients (ISAE 3000 / 3402 / 3410).

articles.text: Profession-agnostic ethics and independence standards for all sustainability assurance practitioners (Volume 2 of the 2026 IESBA Handbook), effective for sustainability assurance engagements for periods beginning on or after 15 Dec 2026.

articles.heading: Sustainability Assurance Ethics & Value-Chain Independence
articles.text:
• Volume 2 of the 2026 IESBA Handbook (effective 15 Dec 2026): applies equally to BOTH professional accountants and non-accountant sustainability assurance practitioners.
• Establishes independence standards equivalent in rigor to Part 4A for sustainability assurance engagements of PIEs, plus tailored independence rules for value-chain entities and using the work of another practitioner or external expert.
